prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly Eric said you wanted to confer before I cut code on Phase A — good call, I have open design questions worth your read first:

1. IDENTIFIER STRATEGY. IP alone is weak (NAT, residential proxies, Tor). Strawman: composite key = sha256(ip || UA || header-order-hash) when available, fall back to ip-only with a confidence penalty. The sensors carry different evidence shapes though — bridge-events has source IP, family-anchor has UA+referrer, admin-audit has user/route. Do we accept that some signals only contribute partial identifiers and the profile gets stitched over time? Or do we hard-require ip+UA before opening a profile?

2. REPLAY MODEL. On startup do we (a) re-read the entire forensic ledger to rebuild all profiles in memory, then tail forward, or (b) only tail forward from current EOF and trust the on-disk profiles to be authoritative? (a) is robust to profile corruption but gets slow as ledger grows. I lean (b) with an explicit `npm run hunt-mode:rebuild` for full replay when needed.

3. STORAGE LAYOUT. .hunt/profiles.jsonl append-only event log (each profile mutation = one line), with a periodic snapshot file .hunt/profiles.snapshot.json? Or just keep the full profile map written atomically on every update (simpler, slower at scale)? I lean append-only event log + snapshot — its how the bridge already works.

4. WHAT TRIGGERS PROFILE CREATION. Every signal? Or only signals above a severity threshold? I lean every signal — the slow-burn probes you mentioned are info-level by design.

Your read on these four, then I cut code.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
